memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: From the descendants of Benjamin... the number was 35,400. From the descendants of Dan... the number was 62,700. From the descendants of Asher... the number was 41,500. From the descendants of Naphtali... the number was 53,400. These were the men counted by Moses and Aaron and the twelve leaders of Israel, each one representing his family. - Num 1:36-44 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The counting continues, and finally all the tribes are accounted for. Every man twenty years and older who was able to serve was numbered. This was, in part, a preparation for the journey and the battles ahead. God was organising a people who would need to be ready — not passive, but prepared to stand and serve.

There is a spiritual lesson here for us. The Christian life is not meant to be lived on the sidelines. God counts His people as those who are ready to serve. Every believer has been given a part to play in God's work, and He calls us to be prepared and willing.

Being "able to serve" did not mean these men were the strongest warriors on their own. Their strength was in the Lord who fought for them. In the same way, our readiness to serve God does not depend on our own great abilities, but on our willingness to be used by Him.

The New Testament describes the Christian life using the picture of a soldier — not fighting with weapons of this world, but standing firm in faith (2 Tim 2:3-4; Eph 6:11). We are called to be spiritually alert and ready.

Are you ready to be counted among those who serve God? He is not looking for the most talented, but the most willing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you living on the sidelines or ready to serve God?
- What holds you back from offering yourself to His work?
- How can you prepare your heart to be used by God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I want to be counted among those ready to serve You. Make me willing, prepare my heart, and use me for Your purposes. Amen.
